A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 29-page versions of the same SPHERE paper, including Appendices A–E. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original sequential-editing experiments, downstream evaluations, runtime measurements, sensitivity analyses, and generation case studies in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains original sequential-editing results for LLaMA3 and Qwen2.5, together with downstream evaluations, runtime measurements, sensitivity analyses, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: SPHERE's principal-direction estimation, projection matrix, and application to editing updates remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D.5. The corrections concern theoretical quantities rather than the editing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate editing on CounterFact and ZsRE and general abilities on GSM8K, RTE, Natural Questions, and BoolQ. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the pre-edited controls and FT, MEMIT, PRUNE, RECT, and AlphaEdit baselines. ROME remains in the Section 3.1 analysis, and comparator membership in the other comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The editing budgets, batch sizes, model configurations, evaluation metrics, and supplementary experimental procedures in Section 5 and Appendix D are unchanged. Equation 8 corrects a theoretical expression; the HE measurement definition in Equation 5 is unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same HE–stability correlation analyses, weight-geometry visualizations, projection-integration studies, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and four generation case studies. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical ± reporting, Figure 2 retains its Spearman correlations and p-values, and Figure 3 retains its confidence displays. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, all result plots, and Appendix E generations are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports LLaMA3/ZsRE efficacy of 90.01±0.21 for SPHERE and 86.64±0.23 for AlphaEdit in both versions.

T1.justification: Equation 7 replaces the new-knowledge variables K1 and V1 with the original-knowledge variables K0 and V0. Equation 8 changes the HE summation from i<j to i≠j, matching Equation 5 and Appendix C.1's Equation 26. Appendix C.1 also replaces εmax∥Δ∥ with εmax∥ΔW∥ in Equation 24. These are localized mathematical corrections; theorem statements and the remaining proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about HE stability, SPHERE, knowledge retention, and editing performance, including the reported 16.41% editing improvement and 38.71% plug-and-play improvement.

C2.justification: The interpretations connecting HE fluctuations to knowledge disruption and projection to editing stability remain unchanged. Equation 7's corrected description matches the original-knowledge interpretation already present in v2's surrounding discussion and Appendix C.1; no new mechanism or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same edited layers, optimization steps, learning rates, projection hyperparameters, hardware, and integration instructions. The project and code access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, the bibliography, and citations to prior research are unchanged. Neither the cited-work coverage nor SPHERE's positioning relative to earlier editing and hyperspherical-uniformity methods changes.

P1.justification: The explanatory sentence following Equation 7 is corrected to identify original knowledge, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose, section ordering, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13, Tables 1–2, and the four appendix case-study displays retain their graphics, structure, captions, and placement. There is no display redesign or page-layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical consistency by making Equation 7 describe disturbance to original knowledge, aligning Equation 8 with the HE convention in Equation 5 and Appendix C.1, and correcting the perturbation norm in Equation 24. These repairs make the existing argument more precise. The gain is limited: Appendix C.2 still uses i<j in Equation 36, so the revision does not fully harmonize the theory.
